ChatGPT Space is a shared workspace where people and AI create and maintain living documents together.

Work often gets scattered across chats, docs, files, and updates. Space keeps context, collaboration, and AI assistance in one place. Instead of treating AI as a separate chat tool, Space lets you tag ChatGPT, Codex, or your dot directly inside a shared page to edit, research, code, or take next steps.

Features

Self-updating pages for writing, visualizing, research, and coding.

Real-time team editing, comments, and AI tagging in the same document.

Shared knowledge hub for files, pages, slides, spreadsheets, and team context. [...] Dots integration to keep pages updated across ChatGPT, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.

Templates for to-do lists, project dashboards, and onboarding-style workflows.

Who it’s for: Teams and professionals on Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans who collaborate on plans, research, projects, and documentation.

Use cases: Build project dashboards, onboarding prototypes, campaign plans, visual research pages, and self-updating to-do lists.

Try Space and see how AI can become part of your team’s workflow.

results.title: Slashspace AI: Canvas first AI experience for sustained, complex work | Product Hunt
results.content:
All the agents see everything in the space. Run multiple agents in parallel, ask them to derive context from one another, and direct them to solve problems that you wouldn't have been able to do in a linear app.   
  
Slashspace is the 10x generalist's interface AI interface. It can write, delegate, plan, code, create, and do many things. If ChatGPT raised the floor on who can build things, Slashspace is meant to raise the ceiling on what's possible for ambitious people and teams to build in the AI-era. [...] I switched to Slashspace after spending way too much time copy-pasting between ChatGPT, Claude, and a pile of browser tabs, and it genuinely changed how I work. The infinite canvas lets you run multiple AI chats side by side, drop in PDFs, websites, and spreadsheets as sources, and connect tools like email and Slack, all without losing context between sessions. Everything is stored locally on your device, which I appreciate since I deal with sensitive documents regularly. The spatial layout takes a little getting used to, but once it clicks, going back to a standard chat interface feels limiting. It is best suited for researchers, writers, or anyone doing deep work across multiple sources and models. Casual users who only need a quick AI response here and there will probably find it more
